"""Cyrillic 'у' detector (the Russian/Ukrainian letter U, as in the preposition у, "at/by").

Layer-1 MLP component 2880 writes into the residual stream mainly when the current token is
the Cyrillic letter у or У. It is strongest when that token is a standalone word or a
word-initial syllable: the preposition " у" (у меня, у вас, у дороги) and the sentence-initial
"У". Inside a word it is weaker (a prefix like у- in уверен, or a syllable like об|у|словлена),
and near zero when it is a case ending (схем|у, автор|у). A Latin "ú"/"u" that plays the same
role in Czech, Slovak and Polish words (ú|činek, u|dogodnie) gives a weak response.

The program looks only at the newest token and the one before it. Its prediction is a
fixed level per case, so it says "this token is у, and how word-initial it is".
"""

READS = ()

STRONG = 10.0    # standalone or word-initial Cyrillic у / У
WEAK = 1.0       # у inside a word, or a case ending
LATIN_U = 1.5    # Latin ú (Czech/Slovak "ú") in the same role


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    letter = token.strip().lower()
    if letter == "у":
        standalone = token[:1] in (" ", "У")
        value = STRONG if standalone else WEAK
    elif letter == "ú":
        value = LATIN_U
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return None, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2881 -- the "under" detector.

This component fires on the spelling of the word "under" as it appears in Russian
(под), Ukrainian (під) and English/Romance/Slavic "pod": the text so far ends with
those letters. It is strongest on Russian "под" (about 13), weaker on Latin "pod"
(about 8, as in iPod, Pod, gastropod, or the Kubernetes pod). It is near zero everywhere
else, with a small negative dip on tokens containing "pain" or "poison".

The program keeps the last few tokens of the current document as text, and predicts the
activation from whether that text now ends in one of the stems.
"""

READS = ()

STEMS = ("под", "під", "pod")   # "under" in Russian, Ukrainian and English/Romance
CYRILLIC_VALUE = 13.0           # typical activation on a completed Cyrillic stem
LATIN_VALUE = 8.0               # typical activation on a completed Latin "pod"
NEGATIVE_WORDS = ("pain", "poison")
NEGATIVE_VALUE = -1.5
WINDOW = 6                      # tokens of text kept, enough to span a split stem


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    start = t
    while start > 0 and start > t - WINDOW and doc[start - 1] == doc[t]:
        start -= 1
    text = "".join(prefix.token_strings[start : t + 1]).lower()
    value = 0.0
    if text.endswith(STEMS):
        value = CYRILLIC_VALUE if text.endswith(("под", "під")) else LATIN_VALUE
    elif any(word in prefix.token_strings[t].lower() for word in NEGATIVE_WORDS):
        value = NEGATIVE_VALUE
    return carry, value

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 2882: a weak, token-specific response.

It is small and mostly unpredictable. Its clearest pattern is on word pieces: it is
negative on many pieces of longer words that are cut into several tokens and continued
by a suffix, such as " provinc" (province), " instit" (institution), " conserv"
(conservative), " educ" (education), " administr" (administration), " constr"
(construction) and " polit" (political). Typical values are about -0.2 to -0.8.

This program marks a sample of those word-piece tokens with -0.1 and predicts 0
everywhere else. It is a hand-picked list of the concept, not an exhaustive one.
"""

READS = ()

STEM_PIECES = {
    " provinc", " instit", " contrib", " anal", " conserv", "istr", " relig", " constr",
    " Instit", " Constit", "onom", "ateg", "ist", " educ", " restaur", " repar",
    " instr", " administr", " Polit", " garant", " automat", " prom", " partic",
    " strateg", " compar", " signific", " introdu", " diagn", " prepar", " conspir",
    " polit", " distrib", " produ", " integ", " domin", " energ", "ific", "olog",
    "ivid", "Person", "arm", "str", "permalink", "Showing", "Tags", "Element", "void",
}
VALUE = -0.1


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return None, (VALUE if prefix.token_strings[-1] in STEM_PIECES else 0.0)

"""Explainer program for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2883 (layer 1 MLP down-projection).

What the component does, in plain terms:
  * Mostly it is a "lone space" unit that pushes negative. The token " " on its own
    (the tokenizer splits off a space in front of a number, and also appears in code
    and prose) gets about -1.75 after a word or punctuation (about -2.4 after a month
    name such as "May ", about -2.0 after a comma), and a weaker about -1.1 after a
    newline, an indent, or a digit. In the training text, about 85% of these spaces
    are followed by a digit, so the unit leans toward "a number may start here".
  * A space that is the very first token of a row is a small positive (+1.1).
  * A rare, very large negative spike: the colon of a "Title:" header that starts a
    new document, i.e. "<|endoftext|>Title:" (about -59). Every such case seen in the
    training sample has this value, so it is predicted as that value.
Everything else is predicted as 0. The program only reads the tokens so far
(READS is empty), and uses no table of token ids.
"""

READS = ()

END_OF_TEXT = "<|endoftext|>"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    cur = tokens[-1]

    if cur == " ":
        if t == 0:
            return carry, 1.1
        prev = tokens[-2]
        if prev.strip() == "" or prev.isdigit():
            return carry, -1.1
        return carry, -1.75

    if cur == ":" and t >= 2 and tokens[-2] == "Title" and tokens[-3] == END_OF_TEXT:
        return carry, -58.97

    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2884, read as a punctuation / quotation-closing detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It is mostly quiet (near 0) on ordinary words, and it goes negative at punctuation
  that ends a unit of text:
  * a closing quotation mark (") ” ” 」 » that ends a quoted span of prose. The
    strongest response comes when the quote closes a span of roughly 6 to 40 tokens;
    a quote that closes a very short span (like "name" or "") barely responds, and
    one that closes a very long span responds less.
  * sentence-final ! ? (and their full-width forms), which respond strongly
    wherever they appear.
  * a semicolon, a vertical bar used as a separator (" |"), an em dash (" —").
  * a line break that follows a word (end of a prose line), weakly.
- An opening straight quote gives a weak negative value.
- Starting a new document (the first token of a packed row, or where the document id
  changes) gives a small positive value.

The program tracks, per document, the position of the last unclosed opening quote,
and the parity of straight double quotes to tell opening from closing.
Its predictions are in activation units (roughly -1 for a strong closing quote).
"""

READS = ()

OPEN_QUOTES = set("“「『«")
CLOSE_QUOTES = set("”」』»")
END_MARKS = set("!?！？")


def quote_weight(distance):
    """How strongly a closing quote responds, by the number of tokens since its opening quote."""
    if distance < 3:
        return 0.0
    if distance < 6:
        return 0.35
    if distance < 10:
        return 0.75
    if distance <= 40:
        return 1.0
    return 0.35


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    new_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_document:
        # first token of a document: a small positive response, state reset
        return (None, 0), 0.3
    open_at, parity = carry if carry else (None, 0)
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    v = 0.0
    if '"' in s:
        if parity % 2 == 1 and open_at is not None:
            v = -quote_weight(t - open_at)  # closes a straight-quoted span
            open_at = None
        else:
            open_at = t  # opens one: a weak negative response
            v = -0.1
        parity += s.count('"')
    elif any(c in CLOSE_QUOTES for c in s):
        if open_at is not None:
            v = -quote_weight(t - open_at)
        open_at = None
    elif any(c in OPEN_QUOTES for c in s):
        open_at = t
    elif any(c in END_MARKS for c in s):
        v = -0.7
    elif s == ";":
        v = -0.35
    elif s == " |":
        v = -0.5
    elif s == " —":
        v = -0.3
    elif s in ("\n", "\n\n") and prefix.token_strings[-2][-1:].isalpha():
        v = -0.2
    return (open_at, parity), v

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 2885: the "print call" detector.

It goes strongly negative on the word that starts a printing / logging call in source code:
`print` in Python, `console.log`, `System.out.println`, `cout <<`, Go's `fmt.Printf`,
C's `echo`, plus the `main` of a `void main` / `int main` definition. Its
activation is near zero everywhere else, including the same words in English prose
("we will print the results" is ~0, `print(...)` in code is about -7).

Plain-language rule used here:
  * find the output-function name on the current token (print, println, printf, echo,
    cout, fmt, puts, console, ...);
  * if it sits in code (not after an ordinary English word), predict its typical strength;
  * `.log` is strong only as `console.log`; `System.out` is strong; `<<` after `cout` is moderate.
Stateless: each position is judged from the current and previous token only.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation of the name when it is used as an output call in code.
CALL_STRENGTH = {
    "print": -7.0,
    "println": -6.0,
    "printf": -5.0,
    "Println": -7.0,
    "Printf": -6.5,
    "echo": -3.5,
    "puts": -4.0,
    "cout": -8.0,
    "fmt": -7.0,
    "console": -3.0,
    "printStackTrace": -3.0,
    "alert": -2.5,
    "stdio": -6.0,
    "iostream": -6.0,
}


def is_english_word(prev):
    """True for an ordinary English word just before, as in 'will print the result'."""
    word = prev.strip()
    keywords = ("int", "void", "func", "return", "import")
    return prev.startswith(" ") and word.isalpha() and word not in keywords


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    name = token.strip().lstrip(".#:")
    after_dot = token.lstrip().startswith(".") or token.startswith("::")

    if name == "out" and prev.endswith("System"):  # System.out.println
        return None, -10.0
    if name == "log" and after_dot and prev.endswith("console"):  # console.log
        return None, -10.0
    if name == "log" and after_dot:
        return None, -1.0
    if name == "main":  # entry point of a C / Java / Go program
        if prev.strip() in ("void", "int"):
            return None, -10.0
        if prev.strip() == "func":
            return None, -5.0
        return None, 0.0
    if name == "<<" and prev.strip() == "cout":  # std::cout << ...
        return None, -4.0
    if name in CALL_STRENGTH and not is_english_word(prev):
        return None, CALL_STRENGTH[name]
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2886 -- the C++ `std::` scope operator detector.

This component writes a large positive value into the residual stream on the `::`
token when it directly follows the identifier `std` (as in `std::vector`,
`std::enable_if_t`, `std::cout`). There its activation is about 13 (typically 11 to
15). On `::` after any other identifier (`Vec::new`, `Model::run`, `io::Read`) it is
small, roughly -0.5 to +1, and the program predicts 0 there.

The program: predict 13 at a `::` whose previous token (in the same document) is
`std`, and 0 everywhere else. It needs no state beyond the current and previous
token.

What it leaves out: the replacement character `�` (a broken byte of a multi-byte
character) takes both signs, from about -6 to +3, depending on the script around
it, and the program predicts 0 there; so does a rare `:` after `Title` at the start
of a document (about 12). Those account for roughly a fifth of the variance the
program misses; most of the rest is the small values on other `::` and on ordinary
tokens.
"""

READS = ()

STD_ACTIVATION = 13.0
SCOPE_TOKEN = "::"
NAMESPACE = "std"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    same_doc = len(tokens) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if same_doc and tokens[-1] == SCOPE_TOKEN and tokens[-2].strip() == NAMESPACE:
        return carry, STD_ACTIVATION
    return carry, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Approximate this component as short English question/request pulses.

An opening word gets a context-dependent strength. Articles, auxiliaries,
pronouns and quantity/classifier words carry the pulse for at most five
following tokens, stopping at ordinary content. Sentence/clause boundaries, a new chat
user turn and recent numbers adjust the opening strength. Other tokens are 0.
"""
import re

READS = ()
GROUPS = {
    'calculation': 'find calculate compute determine estimate evaluate solve derive',
    'creation': 'write create make develop design generate construct implement',
    'explanation': 'show prove explain describe identify illustrate represent',
    'enumeration': 'list name state',
    'giving': 'tell give provide',
    'other': 'where when who whom whose which whether',
}
FAMILY = {w:g for g,words in GROUPS.items() for w in words.split()}
FAMILY.update({w:w for w in ('what','how','why')})
# Lowercase strength and additional strength for an initial capital.
WORD = {
    'find': (-.1, .8), 'calculate': (.2, .2), 'compute': (-.2, -.1),
    'determine': (-.3, 1.2), 'estimate': (0, 1.1),
    'evaluate': (-.2, .7), 'solve': (-.4, .8), 'derive': (-.3, .4),
    'write': (.2, 1.9), 'give': (.1, 1.5),
    'show': (0, .3), 'prove': (.4, 2.4), 'explain': (.5, .6),
    'describe': (0, .8), 'identify': (-.2, .6),
    'what': (.2, .7), 'how': (.3, .3), 'why': (.3, .1),
    'where': (.1, .1), 'who': (0, .5), 'whose': (.1, .5),
    'which': (0, .9), 'when': (0, -.1), 'whether': (0, -.2),
}
# Gains after a sentence, a clause, a newline, or a chat-user label.
BOUNDARY = {
    'what': (2.2, 1.6, .7, 2.1), 'how': (1.6, .8, .4, .9),
    'why': (.5, .7, .1, .3), 'other': (.3, .1, 0, .4),
    'calculation': (2.8, 1.2, 1.0, 1.7),
    'creation': (1.2, .3, .4, 2.3),
    'explanation': (1.4, .8, .5, 0),
    'enumeration': (.4, 0, .3, .9), 'giving': (1.3, .8, -.1, .6),
}
AUX = set(('is are was were do does did can could would should will '
           'may might have has had am').split())
# Each continuation is offset + multiplier * opening strength.
FRAME = {
    'what': {'is': (.2,.9), 'aux': (.2,.4), 'the': (.4,.8),
             'a/an': (.2,.2), 'of': (.4,.5), 'classifier': (.4,.2)},
    'how': {'aux': (.3,.5), 'quantity': (.2,1.5), 'is': (.2,.2)},
    'why': {'aux': (.4,.4)},
    'where': {'aux': (.3,.2)},
    'who': {'is': (0,.2)},
    'which': {'of': (1.3,1.2), 'the': (0,.6)},
    'calculation': {'the': (.2,1.3), 'a/an': (0,.4), 'of': (.4,.6)},
    'creation': {'a/an': (.2,2.3), 'the': (0,.8)},
    'write': {'a/an': (.7,1.7), 'the': (.1,1.2)},
    'explanation': {'determiner': (0,.8), 'the': (0,.7)},
    'giving': {'me': (1,1.4), 'the': (.2,.7), 'a/an': (.1,.7)},
    'enumeration': {'the': (.5,.8), 'determiner': (.4,.6)},
    'inversion': {'pronoun': (.4,.2)},
}
INITIAL = ('', False, -1, -1, (), '', 0.0, 0)


def function_class(w):
    if w == 'is': return 'is'
    if w in AUX: return 'aux'
    if w in ('a','an'): return 'a/an'
    if w in ('the','me','of'): return w
    if w in ('i','you','we','it','they','he','she','us','there'): return 'pronoun'
    if w in ('many','much','long','often','far','old'): return 'quantity'
    if w in ('kind','type','sort','number','value'): return 'classifier'
    if w in ('this','that','some','any','all'): return 'determiner'
    return ''


def advance(state, token):
    prev, cap, boundary, word_start, digits, root, strength, chain = state
    match = re.search(r'[^\W\d_]+$', token)
    raw = match.group() if match else ''
    # Retain case and starting context across pieces such as Pro + ve.
    if raw and token[0].isalpha() and prev and boundary < 0:
        w = prev + raw.lower()
    else:
        w = raw.lower()
        cap = bool(raw and raw[0].isupper())
        word_start = boundary
    value = 0.0
    if w in FAMILY:
        family = FAMILY[w]
        base, capital = WORD.get(w, (0,0))
        strength = base + capital * cap
        if word_start >= 0:
            strength += BOUNDARY[family][word_start]
        if prev == 'to':
            strength += {'calculation': .4, 'explanation': .2,
                         'giving': -.2}.get(family, 0)
        if prev == 'please':
            strength += {'giving': 1.1, 'explanation': .8,
                         'enumeration': .5, 'creation': .3}.get(family, 0)
        if prev in ('in','at','by','for','from') and w == 'what':
            strength += .5
        if sum(digits) >= 2:
            strength += {'what': .8, 'how': .4,
                         'calculation': .4}.get(family, 0)
        strength = max(0.0, strength)
        roots = ('what','how','why','where','who','which','write')
        root = w if w in roots else family
        chain, value = 1, strength
    elif w in AUX and (cap or word_start >= 0):
        strength = .9 if w in ('is','can','does','did','would') else .5
        root, chain, value = 'inversion', 1, strength
    else:
        kind = function_class(w)
        if chain and kind:
            offset, multiplier = FRAME.get(root, {}).get(kind, (0,0))
            value = max(0.0, offset + multiplier * strength)
            chain += 1
        elif token.strip():
            chain = 0
        if chain > 5: chain = 0
    s = token.strip()
    if '\n' in token: boundary = 3 if prev == 'user' else 2
    elif s and s[-1] in '.!?': boundary = 0
    elif s and s[-1] in ',;:': boundary = 1
    elif s: boundary = -1
    digits = (digits + (int(any(ch.isdigit() for ch in token)),))[-32:]
    return (w, cap, boundary, word_start, digits, root, strength, chain), value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    state = INITIAL if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    state, value = advance(state, prefix.token_strings[-1])
    return (doc, state), value
programs.haiku:
"""Question-and-task opener detector (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2887).

The component fires on the word that opens a question or an instruction the
reader has to act on: wh-words ("What", "How", "Which") and imperative task
verbs ("Find", "Write", "Determine", "Calculate", "Solve", "Explain"), and their
equivalents in other languages ("Qué", "Welche", "Qual", "请", "ли", "Как").

It is strongest for such a word at the start of a sentence, much weaker for the
same word mid-sentence, and near zero for it inside code ("findObjects").

It also fires on the small words that follow an opener while the request is
still being phrased: "What *is* *the* ...", "Find *the* ...", "Write *a* ...".
Those words get a decaying share of the opener's strength, up to four words on.

Strength is boosted when there are numbers nearby, as in math exercises
("Let g = 4. What is g + 2?"), where the component is at its largest.

Everything else predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical strength of each opener at the start of a sentence.
OPENERS = {
    "determine": 4.5,
    "write": 3.2,
    "estimate": 3.0,
    "calculate": 3.0,
    "qual": 3.0,
    "what": 2.5,
    "explain": 2.5,
    "give": 2.4,
    "find": 2.2,
    "solve": 1.5,
    "как": 1.8,
    "how": 1.4,
    "welche": 1.7,
    "quelle": 1.2,
    "identify": 1.0,
    "factor": 1.0,
    "can": 0.9,
    "wie": 0.8,
    "make": 0.8,
    "compute": 0.8,
    "哪些": 0.8,
    "is": 0.6,
    "are": 0.6,
    "which": 0.6,
    "ли": 0.6,
    "qué": 0.7,
    "请": 0.7,
    "show": 0.5,
    "describe": 0.5,
    "design": 0.5,
    "generate": 0.5,
    "implement": 0.5,
    "list": 0.4,
    "create": 0.3,
    "¿": 1.1,
}

# Small words that can follow an opener while the request is being phrased.
FOLLOWERS = frozenset(
    "a an the of is are to me some all your this each it its out many much".split()
)

# Share of the opener's strength for the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th following word.
DECAY = (1.0, 0.8, 0.5, 0.3)
MID_SENTENCE = 0.25    # an opener mid-sentence fires at a quarter of its strength
NUMBER_BOOST = 1.7     # applied when the last 40 tokens hold at least 3 digits
NUMBER_MIN = 3
SCALE = 0.7            # overall shrink, fitted on training rows
ENDS_SENTENCE = (".", "?", "!", ":", "\n", '"')


def _word(token):
    return token.strip().strip("*#\"'“”").lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    text = tokens[-1]
    prev = tokens[-2] if len(tokens) > 1 else ""
    new_doc = len(tokens) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if new_doc or carry is None:
        recent, chain_len, chain_level = (), 99, 0.0
    else:
        recent, chain_len, chain_level = carry
    recent = (recent + (text,))[-40:]
    digits = sum(sum(c.isdigit() for c in t) for t in recent)
    at_start = new_doc or prev.endswith(ENDS_SENTENCE) or "\n" in prev
    word = _word(text)
    if word in OPENERS and at_start:
        chain_level, chain_len = OPENERS[word], 0
        value = OPENERS[word]
    elif chain_len < len(DECAY) and word in FOLLOWERS:
        value = chain_level * DECAY[chain_len]
        chain_len += 1
    elif word in OPENERS:
        chain_level, chain_len = OPENERS[word] * MID_SENTENCE, 0
        value = chain_level
    else:
        chain_len, value = 99, 0.0
    boost = NUMBER_BOOST if digits >= NUMBER_MIN else 1.0
    return (recent, chain_len, chain_level), SCALE * boost * value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2889, a "wait" detector.

This component is silent almost everywhere and drops sharply negative on the English
word "wait" (and its inflections "waiting", "waited", "waits"), at the token where the
word appears. Its strongest responses come in self-correcting reasoning text, where
"Wait," opens a new thought ("... 2x = 6. Wait, that is wrong ..."). The size of the
dip depends on the spelling: lowercase " wait" dips the most (about -7.5), capitalised
"Wait" about -5, and the other inflections about -6. Context changes little.

The program is stateless: at each token it looks only at that token's text.
"""

READS = ()

# Word forms of "wait" and their typical activation at the token.
LOWER_WAIT = -7.5      # " wait", "wait"
CAPITAL_WAIT = -5.0    # " Wait", "Wait"
OTHER_FORMS = -6.0     # "waiting", "waited", "waits", "WAIT", "Waiting", ...
OTHER_FORMS_SET = frozenset({"waiting", "waited", "waits", "waiter"})


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    if word == "wait":
        return carry, LOWER_WAIT
    if word == "Wait":
        return carry, CAPITAL_WAIT
    if word.lower() == "wait" or word.lower() in OTHER_FORMS_SET:
        return carry, OTHER_FORMS
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2891: an Arabic verb-prefix detector (negative), with a weak Persian
flip and two Chinese words.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Arabic present-tense verbs carry a one-letter prefix (ت ta-, ي ya-, ن na-, أ a-, س sa-).
  The tokenizer often splits that prefix off as its own token, with a leading space:
  " ت", " ي", " ن", " أ", " س". Some short prefix pieces (" تع", " تن", " تست", ...) behave
  the same way, so they are listed too.
- Right after a particle that introduces a verb (لا, لن, لم, أن, التي, ما, كي, لكي, حتى),
  the component is strongly negative, about -9. Elsewhere it is still negative, but by
  letter: ت about -5, ي about -6, ن about -4, أ about -2.5, س about -1.5.
- The same letters in Persian text have the opposite, weak sign. Persian is spotted by
  letters Arabic does not use (ی ک گ پ چ ژ) in the last 120 tokens of the same document;
  when there are several, the program predicts 0.
- Two Chinese words that open a verb phrase are mildly positive: 可 (可以, 可能) and 怎么.
- Everything else predicts 0. Most of the remaining variance is small, diffuse noise.

The program carries no state beyond the tokens it reads, and never looks past a document
boundary.
"""

READS = ()

# Arabic word-initial verb-prefix pieces, as the tokenizer emits them (leading space).
VERB_PREFIXES = {
    " ت", " ي", " ن", " أ", " س",
    " تن", " تع", " تش", " تح", " تست", " يع", " يف", " يت", " تت", " وت", " تس", " تق", " تم",
    " ست", " تو", " وي", " نت",
}
# Words after which an Arabic verb takes its present or subjunctive form.
VERB_TRIGGERS = {" لا", " أن", " التي", " لن", " لم", " ما", " لكي", " كي", " حتى"}
# Activation for a prefix without a trigger, by its first letter.
LETTER_VALUE = {"ت": -5.0, "ي": -6.0, "ن": -4.0, "أ": -2.5, "س": -1.5}
AFTER_TRIGGER = -9.0
# Letters Persian uses and Arabic does not.
PERSIAN_ONLY = set("یکگپچژ")
PERSIAN_LIMIT = 4  # this many such letters in the recent text means Persian: predict 0
WINDOW = 120  # recent tokens, in the same document, that are checked
CHINESE = {"可": 1.3, "怎么": 1.5}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if cur in CHINESE:
        return None, CHINESE[cur]
    if cur not in VERB_PREFIXES or len(prefix.token_ids) < 2:
        return None, 0.0
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if prefix.document_ids[-2] != doc:
        return None, 0.0
    recent = zip(prefix.token_strings[-WINDOW:-1], prefix.document_ids[-WINDOW:-1])
    persian = sum(ch in PERSIAN_ONLY for s, d in recent if d == doc for ch in s)
    if persian >= PERSIAN_LIMIT:
        return None, 0.0
    if prefix.token_strings[-2] in VERB_TRIGGERS:
        return None, AFTER_TRIGGER
    return None, LETTER_VALUE.get(cur.strip()[:1], -3.0)

"""Opening curly braces, and a few JavaScript tokens, for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2892.

What it does, in plain terms
  The component is a "brace detector" with a sign. It fires on a "{" that opens a
  bracketed block, and the sign says what kind of block it is:
  * Object literal or destructuring opener, in JavaScript-looking code: positive. The
    strongest cases are "const { a, b } = ...", "return {", and "module.exports = {",
    and an object passed as an argument, as in "new Foo({". A brace on the same line as
    the key or comma that introduces it is weaker.
  * Statement-block opener: negative. The cases are a function, if, or class body after
    ")" ("function f() {", "if (x) {"), after "else", "try" or "do", after an arrow
    "=>", and a brace on its own line. An opening "(" or "[" at line end is also
    negative, as the start of such a block.
  * Braces inside strings, JSON, LaTeX and format fields ("{\"", "{}", "_{", "${")
    predict 0, since they do not open code blocks.
  * The tokens ".js", "js", "javascript", ".exports" and " async" are mildly positive,
    as JavaScript file names and module words.
  Everything else predicts 0. The program reads only the text before the current token
  (the last 300 characters of the document, carried from step to step).

Why: the component reads the MLP's hidden state, and on code its large values mostly sit
on braces. Object openers push it up and block openers push it down. The same brace
means different things in JavaScript and in other text, so the object values are
switched on only when recent text looks like JavaScript.
"""
import re

READS = ()

DECLARATION_WORDS = ("const", "let", "var")
BLOCK_WORDS = ("else", "try", "do", "finally")
NOT_CODE_BEFORE = "_^$\\}"
JS_TOKENS = {".js": 2.0, "js": 1.0, " js": 0.6, ".exports": 4.5, "javascript": 2.5, " async": 1.0}
JS_CONTEXT = re.compile(r"\b(const|let|var|function|require|import|export|async|await|this)\b|=>")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tail = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        tail = ""  # a new document starts with no text before it
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if "{" in token:
        value = brace_value(tail, token)
    elif "\n" in token and token.rstrip("\r\n")[-1:] in ("(", "["):
        value = -0.7  # a line ending in an opening bracket, as before a block
    else:
        value = JS_TOKENS.get(token, 0.0)
    return (tail + token)[-300:], value


def brace_value(before, token):
    """Signed activation for a token containing "{", given the text `before` it."""
    i = token.index("{")
    pre, post = token[:i], token[i + 1 :]
    if (pre[-1:] and pre[-1:] in NOT_CODE_BEFORE) or post[:1] in ('"', "}", "{") or post[:1].isalpha():
        return 0.0  # JSON key, LaTeX, template or format brace
    text = (before + pre).rstrip()
    last = text[-1:]  # the character just before the brace
    j = len(text)
    while j > 0 and text[j - 1].isalpha():
        j -= 1
    word = text[j:]  # the word just before the brace, if any
    before_word = text[:j].rstrip(" \t")[-1:]
    newline = "\n" in post
    in_js = JS_CONTEXT.search(before) is not None
    if text.endswith("=>"):
        return -1.2  # arrow function body
    if word in DECLARATION_WORDS and before_word != ")":
        return 8.0  # destructuring pattern: const { a, b } = ...
    if word == "return":
        return 6.0
    if last and last == "(":
        return (5.0 if newline else 4.0) if in_js else 1.0  # object as an argument
    if last and last == "[":
        return 3.5 if in_js else 0.5  # object inside an array
    if last and last in "=:,":
        if in_js:
            return 5.5 if newline else 3.0  # object literal value
        return 2.0 if newline else 0.3
    if last == ")" or word in BLOCK_WORDS:
        return -1.2 if newline else -0.9  # function, if or class body
    if newline and last.isalpha():
        return -1.1  # a block brace on its own line after a header word
    if post.startswith("\\"):
        return -0.7  # escaped code block inside a string
    return 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj, component 2894, as readable token rules.

The component is quiet on most text (typical |activation| well under 0.1). Its large
values come from a few recognisable spots in C-style code, comment headers and tool
calls, plus one Chinese term:

positive
- C type declarations: the struct/enum/union name right after `typedef`
  (`typedef struct`, about +7).
- C header guards: the `_` after `#ifndef` (about +6) or `#define` (about +4).
- Metadata lines of a comment header: the first word after ` *` when it is a Doxygen
  tag (`\\brief`, `\\param`), `Copyright` or `Created` (about +1.9).
- A function named `main` right after its return type (`int main`) (about +1.5).
- The Chinese term 社会主义 (socialism) (about +2.6).
- The indentation at the start of a javadoc line after `/**` (about +0.8).

negative
- The closing ` */` of a block comment (about -2.5; the biggest values are in
  banner-style comments made of stars or line numbers, which this does not track).
- The opening quote of a `"name": "` value, i.e. the function name of a tool call
  (about -1.1).
- `_modules` (about -0.5).
- The first token of a document (after <|endoftext|>), slightly negative (-0.13).

Everything else predicts 0. Values are the typical activations in each context.
"""

READS = ()

TYPE_WORDS = {"int", "void", "def", "static", "public", "char", "bool", "string"}
TYPEDEF_KINDS = {" struct", " enum", " union"}
# (previous token, current token) -> activation
PAIRS = {
    (" *", " \\"): 1.9,
    (" *", " Copyright"): 1.9,
    (" *", " Created"): 1.9,
    (" *", " Licensed"): 1.9,
    ("#ifndef", " _"): 6.0,
    ("#ifndef", " __"): 6.0,
    ("#define", " _"): 4.0,
    ("#define", " __"): 4.0,
}
# current token -> activation
TOKENS = {
    "社会主义": 2.6,
    " */": -2.5,
    " */\n": -0.3,
    "_modules": -0.5,
}
NAME_VALUE_QUOTE = -1.1
DOC_START = -0.13
JAVADOC_INDENT = 0.8
MAIN_AFTER_TYPE = 1.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    cur = toks[-1]
    prev = toks[-2] if len(toks) > 1 else "<|endoftext|>"
    before = toks[-3] if len(toks) > 2 else ""
    if cur == ' "' and prev == '":' and before == "name":
        return None, NAME_VALUE_QUOTE
    if prev == "typedef" and cur in TYPEDEF_KINDS:
        return None, 7.0
    if (prev, cur) in PAIRS:
        return None, PAIRS[(prev, cur)]
    if cur in TOKENS:
        return None, TOKENS[cur]
    if cur.strip() == "" and prev.endswith("/**\n"):
        return None, JAVADOC_INDENT
    if cur in (" main", "main") and prev in TYPE_WORDS:
        return None, MAIN_AFTER_TYPE
    if len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, DOC_START
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2895: a document-start detector for code and markup openers.

Nearly all of this component's activity sits at the first token of a document: the
position right after a <|endoftext|> boundary, or the first token of a row. There it
fires on a few line-break and comment or markup-opening tokens, most strongly "//\\n",
"\\r" and "<!". Two patterns are exact: the ":" in "<|endoftext|>Title:" (about 2.5),
and a run of carriage returns at the very start of a row (about 5.1). Everywhere else
the activation is near zero, with small token-dependent noise (about ±0.05) that this
program does not predict.

Predicted activation, in the component's own units:
  - first token of a document, if it is one of OPENERS: its listed value;
  - any other first-of-document token containing \\r, \\n, /, * or <: 0.2;
  - ":" right after "Title" right after <|endoftext|>: 2.5;
  - a row that so far holds only "\\r" tokens: 5.1;
  - otherwise 0.
"""

READS = ()

END_OF_TEXT = "<|endoftext|>"

# first-of-document openers and their typical activation
OPENERS = {
    "//\n": 6.6,
    "\r": 5.1,
    "<!": 2.8,
    "\x00": 2.0,
    "\r\n": 1.0,
    "/*\r\n": 0.7,
    "*": 0.7,
}
LINE_OPENING_CHARS = "\r\n/*<"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: True while every token so far in this row is a carriage return
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    cur = toks[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    cr_run = (carry is None or carry) and cur == "\r"
    at_doc_start = t == 0 or toks[-2] == END_OF_TEXT
    value = 0.0
    if at_doc_start:
        if cur in OPENERS:
            value = OPENERS[cur]
        elif any(c in LINE_OPENING_CHARS for c in cur):
            value = 0.2
    if t >= 2 and toks[-3] == END_OF_TEXT and toks[-2] == "Title" and cur == ":":
        value = 2.5
    if cr_run:
        value = 5.1
    return cr_run, float(value)

"""A partial spelling/script heuristic, not a predictor of every activation spike.

Latin fragments inserted into Cyrillic prose get a positive contribution,
strongest for short fragments. Uncommon English word fragments containing
Slavic romanization patterns get a negative contribution, with an extra penalty
when the newest fragment itself is a Slavic ending or transliteration spelling.
Only the current Latin word and a fading Cyrillic-context score are carried.
"""
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache

import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
SLAVIC_SPELLING = re.compile(
    r'ov|ev|sk|vich|ich|aya|iya|ii|yy|kh|zh|shch|ts|ya'
)
SLAVIC_FRAGMENT = re.compile(
    r'ov|ev|sk|sky|ski|ovich|vich|ich|aya|iya|ii|yy|kh|zh|ts|ya'
)


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def english_rarity(word):
    return max(0.0, 4.5 - zipf_frequency(word.lower(), 'en')) / 4.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', 0.0)
    _, previous, word, recent_cyrillic = carry
    letters = token.strip()
    latin = bool(letters) and letters.isascii() and letters.isalpha()
    previous_latin = (
        bool(previous) and previous[-1].isascii() and previous[-1].isalpha()
    )
    previous_cyrillic = bool(
        regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Script=Cyrillic}', previous[-1:])
    )
    cyrillic = bool(regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Script=Cyrillic}+', letters))

    # Keep the trailing Latin word, including fragments inside paths/identifiers.
    tail = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', token)
    if tail and tail.start() == 0 and previous_latin:
        word = (word + token)[-60:]
    else:
        word = tail.group() if tail else ''

    value = 0.001
    if latin:
        if previous_cyrillic:
            value += 0.35 / math.sqrt(len(letters))
        if not previous_latin:
            value += 0.48 * recent_cyrillic
        if previous_latin and token.isalpha():
            spelling = min(2, len(SLAVIC_SPELLING.findall(word.lower())))
            ending = bool(SLAVIC_FRAGMENT.fullmatch(letters.lower()))
            value -= english_rarity(word) * (0.11 * spelling + 0.36 * ending)

    recent_cyrillic = 0.8 * recent_cyrillic + 0.2 * cyrillic
    return (doc, token, word, recent_cyrillic), float(value)

"""Transliterated Russian/Ukrainian name fragments (negative), and Latin letters inside Russian text (positive).

What the component does, as far as a short program can say:
- Negative. On a later piece of a word written in Latin letters whose spelling looks like a
  transliterated Russian or Ukrainian name or place (Visokogorsk|ii, dvore|ts|kov,
  Yanovsk|aya, Vynnyts|ya), it dips below zero. The more Slavic spellings the word shows
  (zh, kh, ts, sh, ch, yy, ii, ov, ev, sk, ya, ny, ...), the deeper the dip. The same
  letters in English, French or code stay near zero.
- Positive. A short Latin token standing alone (a letter or abbreviation such as "S", "I",
  "ti") inside Cyrillic text rises above zero.
Everywhere else the prediction is zero.
"""
READS = ()

# Spellings typical of Russian/Ukrainian transliteration, and of English.
SLAVIC = ("zh", "kh", "ts", "sh", "ch", "yy", "ii", "iy", "ov", "ev", "sk",
          "ya", "yu", "yo", "ny", "ko", "ka", "ich", "aya", "oe", "ova", "ovo", "ski", "sky")
ENGLISH = ("th", "ck", "wh", "ght", "tion", "ing", "ll", "ee", "oo", "ou", "ea", "er", "ly", "ed")


def is_latin(s):
    return s.isascii() and s.isalpha()


def is_cyrillic(c):
    return "Ѐ" <= c <= "ӿ"


def mostly_cyrillic(text):
    """True if most letters in the last 300 characters are Cyrillic."""
    letters = [c for c in text[-300:] if c.isalpha()]
    return len(letters) > 0 and sum(is_cyrillic(c) for c in letters) > 0.3 * len(letters)


def slavic_score(word):
    word = word.lower()
    return sum(word.count(m) for m in SLAVIC) - sum(word.count(m) for m in ENGLISH)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    cur = toks[-1]
    if not cur.strip() or not is_latin(cur.strip()):
        return carry, 0.0
    # A short Latin token that starts a word, inside Cyrillic text.
    if cur[:1] == " ":
        if len(cur.strip()) <= 3 and len(toks) > 1 and mostly_cyrillic(prefix.text_prefixes[-2]):
            return carry, 0.24
        return carry, 0.0
    # A later piece of a Latin-letter word: the word so far, read back to its first piece.
    if len(toks) < 2 or not is_latin(toks[-2]):
        return carry, 0.0
    word = cur
    i = len(toks) - 2
    while i >= 0 and is_latin(toks[i]) and toks[i][:1] != " ":
        word = toks[i] + word
        i -= 1
    if i >= 0 and toks[i][:1] == " ":
        word = toks[i].strip() + word
    score = slavic_score(word)
    return carry, -0.1 * max(0, score - 1) ** 2

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2897: a weak component, mostly quiet.

Its activation is near zero almost everywhere. Its large values are rare negative
spikes (down to about -4) inside garbled, keyword-stuffed or word-salad text. This
program does not find those spikes; it captures two smaller, consistent effects:

1. Document start. The first token of each document (in a packed row, where the
   document id changes) is slightly positive, about +0.2 when the scale is tuned.
2. Lowercase, all-lowercase lines. A lowercase word whose line so far has no
   capitalised word is slightly negative, about -0.05. Lines written entirely in
   lowercase are where the negative spikes concentrate; capitalised prose is near zero.

Everything else predicts 0. The scales are small on purpose: larger guesses on
uncertain tokens move the model's output much more than the component does.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START = 0.2
LOWERCASE_LINE_WORD = -0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: whether the current line has a capitalised word so far (None at a row start)
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    new_doc = len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    line_has_cap = False if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    if "\n" in token:
        line_has_cap = False
    if word[:1].isupper():
        line_has_cap = True
    if new_doc:
        return line_has_cap, DOC_START
    if word.isalpha() and word.islower() and not line_has_cap:
        return line_has_cap, LOWERCASE_LINE_WORD
    return line_has_cap, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2898: a word detector for hard-G / J words.

What it does: it spells out the current word across the tokens of a document, so the
pieces "G" + "aming" make "gaming". When that word is one of a few short words with a hard
G or J and a short vowel (gaming, gamer, gam, gym, gut, gig, jam, jaw, gum, germ, gear, gun,
gem, jet, guy, gadget, gull, game), or a plural of one, the component goes negative, by about
1 to 4. It also goes negative on compounds that end in a core stem (microgaming, battlegear,
logjam, foregut). Common words such as "go", "get", "good", "gas" and "gamma" stay near 0,
and so does nearly every other token.

Why: its job in the model is a small, word-specific push on the residual stream. It is
near zero on almost all tokens and large only on these words.

What the simple version leaves out: a word split across several tokens fires about two to
three times harder than the same word as one token (G + aming is about -8.7, gaming about
-2.5), and the "Title:" colon at a document start is about +5. Both are left out to keep
the program short; the word list is a rough per-word average taken from training rows.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation for each whole word, as spelled so far in a document.
WORD_VALUE = {
    "gaming": -3.1, "gamer": -4.0, "gam": -3.3, "gym": -3.3,
    "gut": -3.2, "gig": -3.0, "jam": -2.7, "jaw": -3.5, "gum": -3.8, "germ": -2.8,
    "gear": -1.7, "gun": -1.4, "gem": -1.4, "jet": -1.0, "guy": -0.8,
    "gadget": -1.6, "gull": -1.9, "game": -0.25,
}

# Compound words ending in a core stem get a typical value for that stem.
ENDINGS = {"gaming": -5.0, "gamer": -6.0, "gear": -5.0, "gym": -5.0, "gut": -4.0, "gam": -4.0}


def trailing_letters(text):
    """The letters after the last non-letter character, lowercased."""
    run = ""
    for ch in text:
        run = run + ch.lower() if ch.isalpha() else ""
    return run


def value_of(word):
    if word in WORD_VALUE:
        return WORD_VALUE[word]
    if word.endswith("s") and word[:-1] in WORD_VALUE:
        return WORD_VALUE[word[:-1]]  # plurals: gears, gems, jaws, guys
    for ending, value in ENDINGS.items():
        if word.endswith(ending):
            return value
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the letters of the current word so far, or None at a row's start.
    word = carry or ""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc or token[:1].isspace():
        word = ""  # a space or a new document starts a new word
    token = token.lstrip()
    if token and all(ch.isalpha() for ch in token):
        word += token.lower()  # a piece of a word continues it
    else:
        word = trailing_letters(token)  # punctuation or digits end the old word
    return word, float(value_of(word))

"""Approximate document-opening and formatting transients, not word meanings.

At a document's first token, ASCII and uppercase text tends negative. An
opening 'Title:' field has a particularly negative colon. An opening run
of double middle dots retains its opening value. Ordinary interior
text is approximated by its small mean; its lexical variation is not fitted.
"""
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if first:
        t = s.strip()
        value = -0.07 - 0.25 * t.isascii()
        value += 0.13 * t.isalpha() - 0.17 * t.isupper()
        if t in {',', '.', '-'}:
            value = 0.03
        if s == 'Title':
            value = 0.085
        if s == '··':
            value = -2.118
        return (doc, s == 'Title', s == '··'), value

    title_colon = carry[1] and s == ':'
    dot_padding = carry[2] and s == '··'
    value = -5.122 if title_colon else -0.001
    if dot_padding:
        value = -2.118
    return (doc, False, dot_padding), value
programs.haiku:
"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 2899: a document-start component.

What it does, from the activations on training rows:

* Almost everywhere it is near zero (typical |activation| about 0.03 to 0.05).
* Its large values come at the first token of each document, i.e. the token right
  after a document break (`<|endoftext|>`) or the first token of a row. There it is
  mostly negative, about -0.2 on average, with a spread of about 0.35 that depends on
  which token opens the document and that no simple word class captures.
* Two rare, sharp cases:
  - the colon in a document that opens with the field label "Title:" drives the
    component to about -5.1 (the strongest activation seen);
  - the repeated middle-dot filler token "··" gives a steady -2.1.

This program predicts those three things and zero everywhere else. Only the
document boundaries (document labels) and the token strings are used, so it needs no
state beyond what it can read from the prefix.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Mean activation of a document's first token (over training data).
DOCUMENT_START = -0.21
# The colon that follows a document-opening "Title" label.
TITLE_LABEL = "Title"
COLON = ":"
# Repeated middle-dot filler token.
DOT_LEADER = "··"
TITLE_COLON_VALUE = -5.1
DOT_LEADER_VALUE = -2.1


def _starts_document(prefix, i: int) -> bool:
    """True where token `i` is the first token of its document within the row."""
    return i == 0 or prefix.document_ids[i] != prefix.document_ids[i - 1]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    token = prefix.token_strings[t]
    if token == COLON and t >= 1 and _starts_document(prefix, t - 1):
        if prefix.token_strings[t - 1] == TITLE_LABEL:
            return carry, TITLE_COLON_VALUE
    if token == DOT_LEADER:
        return carry, DOT_LEADER_VALUE
    if _starts_document(prefix, t):
        return carry, DOCUMENT_START
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 2901: a sparse, mostly token-level detector.

Most of this component's output is near zero. It moves noticeably only in a few
recognisable situations, and this program predicts those and leaves the rest at 0:

- A sentence opener glued onto the previous sentence's full stop, as in "...census.The"
  or "...year.It" (the period and the capitalised English word arrive as one token or
  with no space between them). Strongly negative.
- The word after a chat turn marker, "<|im_start|>assistant": negative.
- The first token of a document (a new packed document, or the start of a row), where the
  activation depends only on the token itself. Mildly positive for words, near 0 for digits
  and punctuation.
- A single digit that follows a colon or a letter (ratios and labels like "1:2", subscripts
  like "x2"): mildly negative.
- A run of two middle dots "··" (filler in tables of contents or leader lines): strongly
  positive.

    "The", "It", "In", "He", "She", "They", "This", "We", "There", "A", "I", "On",

        return carry, 2.3

It sits near 0 almost everywhere and goes strongly negative on a vowel letter that
spells the diphthong "ae" or "oe" inside a word, as in Latin, Scandinavian, German or
French-style spelling: Petra|e, barba|e, VA|E, Mur|æ|nidæ, insula|e, Gra|ë|t.

- æ / Æ, the ligature (about -6); œ / Œ (about -4).
- An "e" or "E" that joins the previous token and that token ends in "a" or "A", so the
  pair "ae" is split across two tokens (about -6). Other e-initial pieces after such an "a"
  (en, er, es, ...) are weaker (about -3).
- A short token (up to 4 letters) containing "ae" or "AE" that joins the previous token
  (ae, aed, ael, AE, aer) (about -4.4); the same token after a space is weaker (about -1.3).
  Longer English words with "ae" (Michael, Israel, aerial, algae) are left at 0.
- "oe" or "hoe" joined to the word (about -1.8); a joined "e" after "o" (about -0.9).
- Umlauts written as a single letter, ä, Ä, ë, joined to the word (about -1.7).

Anything else, including an "e" that starts a new word (" e"), is 0. The values are the
group means, so this is a rule with its magnitudes measured, not a fitted table.
"""

READS = ()

AE_LIGATURE = {"æ", "Æ"}
OE_LIGATURE = {"œ", "Œ"}
UMLAUT = {"ä", "Ä", "ë"}
OE_TOKEN = {"oe", "hoe", "Oe"}

    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    cur = raw.strip()
    joined = raw[:1] != " "  # the token continues the word before it
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    after_a = prev[-1:].lower() == "a"
    after_o = prev[-1:].lower() == "o"

    elif cur in OE_LIGATURE:

        value = -6.0 if cur in ("e", "E") else -3.0
    elif "ae" in cur.lower() and len(cur) <= 4:
        value = -4.4 if joined else -1.3
    elif cur in OE_TOKEN and joined:
        value = -1.8
    elif after_o and joined and cur in ("e", "E"):
        value = -0.9
    elif cur in UMLAUT and joined:
        value = -1.7
    return None, value

"""F/PH spellings, with an echo through the rest of a split word.

Short F-containing pieces are strongest; common English words are quieter,
particularly 'of'. Transliteration extends the rule to other scripts, with a
smaller response for Chinese/Japanese text. Word breaks and case transitions
stop the echo. A separate correction handles the first token of a document.
This is a spelling/sound-family approximation, not an exact pronunciation rule.
"""
import math
import re
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency
import regex

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def spelling(text):
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', text)
    letters = ''.join(c for c in s if c.isalpha())
    low = letters.lower()
    transliteration = anyascii(letters).lower()
    special = text.startswith(('<|', '</'))
    latin = not special and ('f' in low or 'ph' in low)
    foreign = not special and not latin and (
        'f' in transliteration or 'ph' in transliteration)
    asian = foreign and bool(regex.search(
        r'\p{Script=Han}|\p{Script=Hiragana}|\p{Script=Katakana}', s))
    n = len(letters)
    first_f = low.find('f') if 'f' in low else low.find('ph')
    last_f = low.rfind('f') if 'f' in low else low.rfind('ph') + 1
    value = 0.015
    if latin:
        frequency = zipf_frequency(low, 'en')
        space = text[:1].isspace()
        value += (1.087 + 0.682 / math.sqrt(max(n, 1))
                  - 0.094 * space - 0.1335 * frequency
                  + 0.475 * (frequency > 0) - 0.105 * min(first_f, 10)
                  + 0.898 * (n == 1) + 0.360 * (n == 2)
                  - 0.498 * ('ph' in low and 'f' not in low))
        if space:
            if low == 'of':
                value -= 1.190
            elif low in ('before', 'therefore'):
                value -= 0.637
            elif low in ('for', 'from', 'if', 'after', 'off', 'self'):
                value -= 0.314
    elif foreign:
        value += 0.776 if asian else 1.498 + 0.971 * (n == 1)
    return value, letters, first_f, last_f, latin, foreign, asian


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    value, letters, first_f, last_f, latin, foreign, asian = spelling(text)
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if first:
        carry = (doc, 0., 0, False, '')
        value -= 0.255
        if latin:
            value -= 2.08 - 0.313 * min(first_f, 10) + 2.62 * (len(letters) == 1)
    _, echo, distance, capitals, previous = carry

    # Continue a word, including dotted initials but not CamelCase boundaries.
    joined = bool(re.match(r'(?:[^\W_]|\ufffd)', text))
    joined |= (capitals and len(previous) <= 2
               and bool(re.match(r'\.[A-Za-z]', text)))
    if text[:1].isupper() and previous and not capitals:
        joined = False
    if text[:1].isdigit() and len(previous) > 2 and not capitals:
        joined = False
    if not joined:
        echo = 0.
    if not latin and not foreign and echo:
        value += echo * (0.585 + 1.073 * math.exp(-0.3 * distance)
                         + 0.106 * capitals)

    # PH can straddle a token boundary: e.g. a piece ending P, then H...
    split_ph = (not first and text[:1].lower() == 'h'
                and prefix.token_strings[-2][-1:].lower() == 'p')
    if split_ph:
        value += 1.606
    if latin or split_ph:
        echo = 1.
        distance = max(0, len(letters) - (last_f if latin else 0) - 1)
    elif foreign and not asian:
        echo, distance = 1., 0
    elif asian:
        echo = 0.
    else:
        echo *= 0.7
        distance += len(letters)
    if not re.search(r'(?:[^\W_]|\ufffd)$', text):
        echo = 0.
    return (doc, echo, distance, letters.isupper(), letters), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2914 -- an "f" detector.

The component fires on the letter f (or the sound /f/ written another way) in the
token being read and in the word being written, and stays quiet elsewhere.
Predicted activation at each token:

  * 2.3 for a bare f-fragment: a token of at most two letters, the first an f,
    punctuation aside: "f", " f", "F", "fa", "fl", "ff", "(f", "-f". Also
    Cyrillic ф, Arabic ف, the ligatures ﬁ ﬂ and long s ſ, read as f.
  * 1.1 for any other token containing an f: "file", " function", "if", "ref",
    "def", "self", "fmt".
  * 1.1 for a later piece of a word that already had an f, while the word goes on:
    " fa" then "ud" (faudrait), "forma" then "ient".
  * 0.7 for "ph", an f-sound; 0.65 for common f-words such as " for", " from",
    " first", " four", which the component follows only weakly.
  * 0 for " of" (the most frequent f-token, which the component ignores), for
    special tokens such as <|endoftext|>, and for every token with no f.

starts with a letter and has no leading space is glued onto the previous token's
word and continues it; any other token starts a new word. A new document resets it.
"""
READS = ()

# Words whose f the component mostly ignores.
PLAIN_WORDS = {' of', ' OF', ' before', ' left', ' therefore', ' significant'}
# Common f-words the component follows only weakly.
COMMON_F_WORDS = {'for', 'from', 'first', 'four', 'five', 'after', 'different',
                  'information', 'few'}
# Letters read as the sound /f/ in other scripts or ligatures.
F_SOUND_OTHER = set('фﬁﬂſف')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    in_f_word = bool(carry)
    if prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        in_f_word = False  # a new document starts a new word

    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    core = text.strip().lower()
    if core.startswith('<|'):
        return False, 0.0  # special tokens

    letters = ''.join(ch for ch in core if ch.isalpha())
    other_f = any(ch in F_SOUND_OTHER for ch in core)
    has_f = 'f' in core or other_f
    continues = text[:1].isalpha()  # glued onto the previous token's word

    if text in PLAIN_WORDS:
        value = 0.0
    elif has_f and len(letters) <= 2 and (letters[:1] == 'f' or other_f):
        value = 2.3  # bare f-fragment
    elif has_f and core in COMMON_F_WORDS:
        value = 0.65
    elif has_f:
        value = 1.1  # an f inside a word or word piece
    elif continues and in_f_word:
        value = 1.1  # a later piece of a word that has an f
    elif 'ph' in core:
        value = 0.7
    else:
        value = 0.0

    if continues:
        in_f_word = in_f_word or has_f
    else:
        in_f_word = has_f and text not in PLAIN_WORDS
    return in_f_word, value

with nothing between them, as in "USPQ", "PQR", "p/q" or "p q"; when an "ap" piece follows a P,

and on a Q after another capital letter. It is negative on "with" after "up" (come up with), on
Cyrillic "ад" after "п" (падение), on "db" after "P" (PDB), and on Thai "ัก" after "พ".

in order, so the first one that matches decides.

    cur = toks[-1]
    word = cur.strip()
    same_doc = len(toks) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = toks[-2] if same_doc else ""
    before = prev.strip()
    after_p = prev.endswith(("P", "p"))
    value = 0.0
    if after_p and word.lstrip("/")[:1] in ("Q", "q"):
        value = 3.5
    elif after_p and word.lower().startswith("ap"):
        value = 2.5
    elif after_p and word.lower().startswith("db"):
        value = -5.5
    elif word.lower() in ("pap", "papa", "pq"):
        value = 3.0
    elif word.endswith("quet") and before.endswith("par"):
        value = 4.3
    elif word == "贺":
        value = 5.0
    elif word in ("q", "Q") and before in (",", "and", "or", "+", "&", "/"):
        value = 1.2
    elif word == "Q" and prev[-1:].isupper():
        value = 0.3
    elif word == "with" and before == "up":
        value = -1.8
    elif word.startswith("ад") and prev.lower().endswith("п"):
        value = -3.0
    elif word.startswith("ัก") and prev.endswith("พ"):
        value = -6.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""A dictionary-based approximation to Japanese/Korean action-noun activation.

Kana marks Japanese context. Kanji whose Chinese translation is a verb, or
whose Japanese gloss describes an operation, use, or necessity, get positive
scores. Two-kanji action compounds split across tokens get a completion bonus;
superlative/ranking meanings get a negative score. Tokens with an extra
non-kanji prefix are attenuated. Korean recognizes common uninflected action-noun stems.
This describes broad meanings, not the component's exact lexical preferences.
"""
import codecs
import re
from functools import lru_cache

import regex
import jmdict
import cedict
import wordnet

READS = ()

ACTION = set('''preparation arrangements attention notice care caution
possession ownership operation action activity opening release publication
 disclosure display expression representation progress advance reduction decline
entry participation start beginning posting submission treatment supply provision
agreement promise contract calculation'''.split())
INFORMATION = set('''search selection specification designation display record
recording registration showing presentation exhibition assignment'''.split())
OPERATIONS = set('''
operation construction creation completion production implementation enforcement
accomplishment management provision acquisition request reference confirmation
execution maintenance preparation use participation release cancellation
permission approval support protection preservation improvement restriction
limitation designation specification selection renewal updating addition
incorporation development treatment processing manufacture communication
'''.split())
MODAL = set('''possible potential feasible necessary needed essential
indispensable need requirement ability permission'''.split())
RANKING = {'number one', 'first', 'first place', 'most', 'best'}


def clean(gloss):
    return re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '', gloss).strip().lower()


@lru_cache(maxsize=20000)
def dictionary_scores(word):
    glosses = jmdict.glosses(word)
    head = clean(glosses[0]) if glosses else ''
    head_words = set(re.findall(r'[a-z]+', head))
    base_words = head_words | set().union(*(wordnet.base_forms(w)
                                           for w in head_words))
    all_words = set(re.findall(r'[a-z]+', ' '.join(glosses[:4]).lower()))
    chinese = cedict.glosses(word)
    chinese_head = clean(chinese[0]) if chinese else ''
    is_verb = len(word) >= 2 and chinese_head.startswith('to ')
    instrumental_use = 'exploit' in re.findall(r'[a-z]+', chinese_head)
    operation = bool(head_words & OPERATIONS)
    main = (1.60 * is_verb + 2.22 * operation
            + 3.46 * instrumental_use + 2.36 * bool(base_words & MODAL)
            - 2.80 * (head in RANKING))
    completion = (0.93 * bool(all_words & ACTION)
                  + 3.04 * bool(all_words & INFORMATION) + 1.68 * operation)
    return main, completion


# Common Korean action nouns, before inflections of "do" or "become".
KOREAN_USE = set('사용 이용 활용 운용 적용'.split())
KOREAN_MODAL = set('필요 가능'.split())
KOREAN_ACTION = set('''
진행 작성 수행 구성 선택 제공 참여 표현 시작 확인 시행 포함 발생 작업
지원 출력 개최 생산 비교 입력 노력 결정 질문 소개 발견 연구 연결
설명 준비 설치 표시 계약 체결 계산 소비 증가 감소 공개 운영 관리
검색 기록 저장 등록 실행 생성 수정 해결 유지 요청 완료 전달 응답
승인 분석 개발 처리 구입 구매 제출 배포 배치 보호 보장 보유 검토
평가 모집 변경 변환 설정 조정 통제 취소 수용 제한 추천 방문 이동
'''.split())
KOREAN_THOUGHT = set('존재 생각 이해 인식 고려 상상'.split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, b'', False, '')
    _, pending, japanese, tail = carry
    raw = pending + prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    text, used = codecs.utf_8_decode(raw, 'replace', False)
    pending = raw[used:]
    korean = bool(regex.search(r'\p{Hangul}', text))
    if regex.search(r'\p{Hiragana}|\p{Katakana}', text):
        japanese = True
    if korean:
        japanese = False
    tail = (tail + text)[-2:]
    value = 0.
    if japanese:
        match = regex.search(r'\p{Han}+$', text)
        if match:
            word = match.group()
            value = dictionary_scores(word)[0]
            if (len(word) == 1 and regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Han}{2}', tail)
                    and jmdict.glosses(tail)):
                value += dictionary_scores(tail)[1]
            if text != word:
                value *= 0.5
    elif korean:
        for stems, score in ((KOREAN_USE, 4.5), (KOREAN_MODAL, 2.7),
                             (KOREAN_ACTION, 2.2), (KOREAN_THOUGHT, 3.0)):
            if tail in stems:
                value = score
                break
    return (doc, pending, japanese, tail), float(value)

fires it is reading the word being written: the letters since the last space or
punctuation mark, lower-cased, which `step` keeps in `carry`. Its sign depends on the
consonant in front of the "ay"/"ai" sound:

  * "bay" at the end of a word (Bay, bay, Kobayashi)   -> strongly negative (about -7)
  * "bhai" (Indian name suffix)                        -> strongly negative
  * "бай" at the end (the same sound in Cyrillic)      -> negative
  * "bay" or "bai" elsewhere in a word                 -> weakly negative
  * "hay" at the end                                   -> negative
  * "laid"                                             -> strongly positive (about +4.6)
  * "lay", "lays", "laying", "lai" as the whole word   -> positive (about +4)
  * "clay", "delay", "slay", "...lay", "...lai" endings -> positive (about +2.2)
  * "dai" / "dail" endings                             -> positive
  * "day" as the whole word                            -> slightly positive
  * words containing "play", "relay" or "rlay" (play, display, replay, relay,
    overlay) are exceptions and stay at zero.

the sign is the main thing a reader should take from this.

import re

READS = ()

# (pattern, value): the first pattern that matches the current word sets the prediction.
RULES = [
    (r"play|relay|rlay", 0.0),  # play, display, replay, relay, overlay: exceptions
    (r"bay$", -7.0),
    (r"bhai$", -6.5),
    (r"бай$", -5.0),
    (r"bay|bai", -1.5),
    (r"hay$", -2.5),
    (r"laid$", 4.6),
    (r"^la(i|y|ys|ying)$", 4.0),
    (r"la(i|y|ys|ying)$", 2.2),
    (r"^day$", 0.4),
    (r"dai(l)?$", 2.6),
]


def _value(word):
    for pattern, value in RULES:
        if re.search(pattern, word):
            return value
    return 0.0

    # carry: the current word so far (letters only, lower-cased), or None at a row's start.

    else:

the token that completes the word. Values are the typical activations measured
on training text."""

WASTE = -5.5  # waste, wasted, wasting, wastes, 废, 废物

    "squander": SPEND, "squandering": SPEND,
    "waste": WASTE, "wastes": WASTE, "wasted": WASTE, "wasting": WASTE,

What it does, in plain terms:
  1. It is strongly positive on the ".com" of a "github.com" URL or Go import path

  2. It is negative on the first token of a document (the token right after
     <|endoftext|>, which packed rows use to join documents), and on the first token
     of a row (no context at all): about -0.35 and -0.25.
  3. Everywhere else it is a small, context-dependent wobble (std about 0.06) that
     this program does not model, so it predicts 0 there.

Only the rules above are used, and each one is a readable concept, not a lookup table.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

GITHUB_TOKEN_PART = "github"   # a "github" piece of the preceding token (e.g. "github", "ithub")
DOCUMENT_START = "<|endoftext|>"
DOTCOM = ".com"

ROW_START_VALUE = -0.25        # first token of a packed row
DOC_START_VALUE = -0.35        # first token after <|endoftext|>
GITHUB_DOTCOM_VALUE = 1.7      # ".com" right after "github"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0:
        return None, ROW_START_VALUE
    previous = strings[t - 1]
    if previous == DOCUMENT_START:
        return None, DOC_START_VALUE
    if strings[t] == DOTCOM and GITHUB_TOKEN_PART in previous:
        return None, GITHUB_DOTCOM_VALUE

It fires on short tokens spelled "al" (" al", "al", " all", "All", "alk", "ali", "alt"),
the same sound in Cyrillic ("ал", "аль") and weakly on longer "al-" words and the Arabic
article "ال". At the first token of each document (row start included) it gives a small
negative value.
"""

READS = ()
START_VALUE = -0.2
SHORT_AL = 0.7
LONG_AL = 0.15


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        return carry, START_VALUE
    w = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if w.startswith("al") or w.startswith("ал") or w.startswith("аль"):
        return carry, SHORT_AL if len(w) <= 4 else LONG_AL
    if w.startswith("ال"):
        return carry, LONG_AL
    return carry, 0.0

"""Velar-consonant fragment detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2926.

What it does: the component fires on a word piece that the tokenizer split off from the
middle of a word, when that piece carries a hard "k" sound. The strongest pieces are
"sk" / "sc" clusters (also Cyrillic "ск"), then "k", "q", Cyrillic "к", and last "c".
Typical cases are names and loanwords cut into pieces: "Mos|k|va", "Tos|k|ana",
"pes|q|", "Tus|c|ia", "sun|sc|ald", "Michaś|ka". It is quiet on whole words and on word-initial
pieces (a piece after a space). Pieces inside code identifiers are not excluded, and they
average lower than names; the rule does not model that.

How the value is set: a piece's activation falls off with its length in characters. A
2-letter "sk" piece averages about 2.5, a 4-letter one about 0.7, and a long one about 0.2.
"k" and "q" pieces are weaker (about 0.5 at 1 letter, 0.04 from 4 letters on). "c" pieces are
the weakest. Everything else predicts 0. The numbers are per-class means read off a few
thousand training rows, so the rule is a readable summary, not a table of token ids.

What it leaves out: most of the variance sits in rare spikes whose size depends on the
surrounding word (whether it is a foreign name, and so on), which the rule can't see. A
per-token-id table would add a little, but it would not be a readable explanation.
"""

import re

READS = ()

SK_SC = re.compile(r"sk|sc|ск")
K_LIKE = re.compile(r"[kqк]")
C_ANY = re.compile(r"c")
LETTER = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]")

# mean activation by piece length in characters (index = length - 1; last value for longer)
SK_BY_LENGTH = (2.5, 2.5, 1.8, 0.7, 0.2)
K_BY_LENGTH = (0.54, 0.31, 0.24, 0.04)
C_BY_LENGTH = (0.38, 0.17, 0.11, 0.05, 0.02)


def by_length(table, n):
    return table[min(n, len(table)) - 1]


def is_inside_word(prev, cur):
    """cur is a word piece that continues a word: no leading space, has a letter, and prev ends in a letter."""
    return (not cur[:1].isspace()) and bool(LETTER.search(cur)) and bool(LETTER.search(prev[-1:]))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    if len(tokens) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    cur, prev = tokens[-1], tokens[-2]
    if not is_inside_word(prev, cur):
        return carry, 0.0
    piece = cur.lower().strip()
    n = len(piece)
    if SK_SC.search(piece):
        value = by_length(SK_BY_LENGTH, n)
    elif K_LIKE.search(piece):
        value = by_length(K_BY_LENGTH, n)
    elif C_ANY.search(piece):
        value = by_length(C_BY_LENGTH, n)
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

What it responds to: the second word of a two-word phrase or compound whose
first word is "work", "wave", "web", "write" or "code". Examples: "work out",
"working out", "work through", "work around", "work flow", "workload",
"workout", "waveform", "wave form", "web hook", "webhook", "write down",
"code base". The same words on their own (e.g. "out", "form", "flow") stay

"work together / work as / works fine / work to".

positive value, which the training data shows on average.

(only inside the same document). A single compound token is looked up in
WORDS, a two-token phrase in PAIRS; anything else is 0. Strengths are rounded
averages of the activations measured on training text, in the same units as
the component's activation (roughly -2 to 9)."""

# Two-token phrases: (first word, second word) -> strength.

        (first, "flow"): 4.5, (first, "through"): 3.5, (first, "around"): 3,
        (first, "from"): 2.5, (first, "station"): 3, (first, "shop"): 1,
        (first, "together"): -1.2, (first, "as"): -1.2, (first, "to"): -1.2,
        (first, "fine"): -1.5, (first, "well"): -1.0, (first, "hard"): -1.0,
    })
PAIRS.update({
    ("write", "down"): 2.2, ("write", "out"): 2.2, ("write", "up"): 2.2,
    ("wrote", "down"): 2.2, ("wrote", "out"): 2.2, ("written", "down"): 2.2,
    ("wave", "form"): 8, ("wave", "forms"): 8, ("wave", "function"): 2,
    ("web", "form"): 3, ("web", "hook"): 4, ("web", "page"): 1.5,
    ("web", "pages"): 2, ("web", "server"): 1.2, ("web", "site"): 1,
    ("code", "base"): 2.6,
    ("problem", "statement"): -1.7, ("java", ".sql"): -2.2,
})

# Single tokens that are themselves compounds.
WORDS = {
    "workload": 6, "waveform": 6, "workaround": 4, "workout": 3, "workouts": 3,
    "workflow": 2, "workflows": 2, "webhook": 4, "webform": 3.5, "workplace": 1,
}

DOC_START = 0.2  # first token of a document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token: the strength of the phrase or word it completes."""
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    value = WORDS.get(cur, 0.0)
    if len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        value = value or DOC_START
    else:

"""Approximate a productive agent/instrument suffix signal.

Join the current ASCII-letter word across tokens. Look for -er/-or nouns that can
be made from an English verb, allowing spelling changes and compounds.
Uncommon formations split across tokens are strongest; familiar whole words
are weak. Word frequencies in other languages suppress some false matches.
Some dictionary non-agent noun classes get a small negative value.
The Chinese device/instrument suffix 器 also gets a positive value.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def properties(word):
    w = word.lower()
    if w.endswith('s'):
        w = w[:-1]
    cats = wordnet.categories(w)
    roots = set()
    for suffix in ('er', 'or', 'ster', 'eer'):
        if w.endswith(suffix) and len(w) > len(suffix) + 1:
            stem = w[:-len(suffix)]
            roots.update((stem, stem + 'e'))
            if len(stem) > 2 and stem[-1] == stem[-2]:
                roots.add(stem[:-1])
            if stem.endswith('i'):
                roots.add(stem[:-1] + 'y')
    def is_verb(r):
        return ('verb' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(r)
                and r in wordnet.base_forms(r))
    verbs = [r for r in roots if is_verb(r)]
    if not verbs:
        # Compound agent nouns can have another word before the verb stem.
        verbs = [r[i:] for r in roots for i in range(1, len(r) - 3)
                 if is_verb(r[i:])]
    stem_frequency = max((zipf_frequency(r, 'en') for r in verbs), default=0.)
    frequency = zipf_frequency(w, 'en')
    foreign = max(zipf_frequency(w, lang)
                  for lang in ('de', 'fr', 'es', 'pt', 'it', 'nl'))
    return cats, stem_frequency, frequency, foreign - frequency


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    match = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', tail + token)
    tail = match[0][-80:] if match else ''
    value = 0.8 if token == '器' else 0.002
    match = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', token)
    ending = r'(?:[eoa]rs?|[eo]red|[eo]ring)$'
    if not match or not re.search(ending, match[0].lower()):
        return (doc, tail), value
    letters = match[0]
    word = re.search(r'[A-Z]?[a-z]+$|[A-Z]+$', tail)[0]
    split = len(letters) < len(word)
    cats, stem_freq, word_freq, foreign = properties(word)
    role = bool(cats & {'noun.person', 'noun.artifact'})
    nonagent = bool(cats & {'noun.body', 'noun.location', 'noun.animal'})
    if letters.lower().endswith(('ered', 'ored', 'ering', 'oring')):
        value = -0.1 if split else 0.002
    elif ('noun.quantity' in cats and not stem_freq) or (nonagent and not role):
        value = -0.3 if split else -0.08
    elif not stem_freq:
        value = 0.25 if split and role else 0.002
    elif not split:
        value = 0.08 if stem_freq > word_freq else 0.002
    elif stem_freq < word_freq or foreign > 3:
        value = 0.002
    elif stem_freq - word_freq <= 1:
        value = 0.4
    elif stem_freq > 5.5:
        value = 0.08
    elif stem_freq > 5:
        value = 0.4
    else:
        value = 1.16 if foreign < -0.75 else 0.66
    return (doc, tail), value

pieces that end in -or/-er but are not agents: "factor", "ocker", "eder".
Each ending's value is its mean activation in training text."""

"""Long-s and double-s spellings in German and Romance text (layers.1.mlp.down_proj:2931).

What it does: this component writes into the residual stream when the current token
spells the voiceless "s" sound with a letter other than plain English s: ß or ſ (long s),
ss, or SS. The strongest cases are word-internal German or Romance pieces such as
"Begräbnis|sen", "Gewis|sen", "Genos|sen", "Mes|sina", "Mendels|sohn", "Rus|se". Short
fragments se, so, ser, sen, son fire more weakly. English ss (less, class, process,
message) stays near zero, while uppercase acronyms with SS (SSL, SSC) fire in any text.

How: for each token the program first asks what s-spelling it contains (ß/ſ, a
final or -iss- ss, another ss, or a short fragment). It then asks whether the text so far
in this document is mostly German or Romance (counting function words such as der, die,
und, le, la, di, che, versus the, and, of). In German or Romance text the value is the
full strength; in English text it is small. Everything else is 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

NON_ENGLISH = set(
    "der die das und nicht ist ein eine sich auf mit von dem den des für auch wie zu im es dass sind "
    "le la les et des est une pour que qui dans pas sur du au "
    "di che il per sono della non una con anche gli el los las en por para es uma não os as dos é com em".split()
)
ENGLISH = set("the and of to is that with for it as was on are by this be from or have an not at which but they".split())
SHORT_S = re.compile("^(se|so|ser|sen|son)$")


def strength(token, german):
    """Predicted activation of one token, given whether the text so far is German/Romance."""
    if "ß" in token or "ſ" in token:
        return 1.5 if german else 0.7
    if "SS" in token:
        return 0.95  # uppercase acronyms (SSL, SSC) fire in any text
    if re.search("iss|sson|ss$", token):
        return 1.5 if german else 0.2
    if "ss" in token:
        return 0.8 if german else 0.1
    if SHORT_S.match(token):
        return 0.4 if german else 0.0
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    foreign, english = (0, 0) if (new_doc or carry is None) else carry
    value = strength(token, foreign > english)
    word = token.lower()
    if word in NON_ENGLISH:
        foreign += 1
    elif word in ENGLISH:
        english += 1
    return (foreign, english), value
